title: Sex Expression, Reproductive Morphology and Pollination Risk

content.overview: Reproductive morphology must be interpreted from observable floral structures. Accurate sex-expression observations support crop planning, breeding, seed production, and pollination-risk management without relying on cultivar labels or assumptions about seed type.

vocabulary.definition: Bearing male reproductive structures that produce pollen.
Bearing female reproductive structures associated with ovule-bearing flowers.
Male and female reproductive structures occurring on the same individual plant.
Transfer of pollen to receptive female reproductive tissue, enabling fertilization when compatible.

sections.title: Identify structures, not labels
sections.body: Sex expression should be documented from visible reproductive morphology. Marketing categories, seed source, or cultivar name do not replace inspection of actual floral structures.

sections.title: Expression can change the crop objective
sections.body: Pollen-producing structures matter because they can alter whether a crop remains unseeded, produces seed intentionally, or requires isolation. Their significance depends on the cultivation objective and neighboring reproductive plants.

sections.title: Inspection should be repeated
sections.body: Reproductive structures do not all appear at the same moment. Repeated observations at multiple nodes and developmental stages provide stronger evidence than a single early inspection.

workedExamples: If a plant was grown from a seed sold as feminized but develops pollen-producing structures, record the observed morphology rather than treating the label as definitive.
If a breeding plant is intentionally producing pollen, document its location and separation strategy relative to receptive plants.
commonMistakes: Assuming seed category guarantees later sex expression.
Making a permanent classification from one ambiguous early structure.
Ignoring pollen movement when reproductive plants share air or outdoor space.
content.practicalApplication: Inspect representative nodes with adequate magnification, document the structure and date, repeat observations as flowering develops, and connect any pollen-producing tissue to the crop's pollination-control plan.
content.summary: Reliable reproductive management begins with observable morphology. Sex expression should be monitored over time and connected directly to pollination risk, crop purpose, and breeding plans.
